   180→### Integration with Existing 3D Camera Control Nodes

   182→ComfyUI already has a camera data pipeline. CarWash-2 should plug into it, not replace it.
   183→
   184→**What exists today:**
   185→```
   186→Load3D node (built-in core)
   187→  → Loads .gltf/.glb/.obj/.fbx/.stl
   188→  → Three.js viewport in the node UI
   189→  → Outputs: IMAGE, MASK, NORMAL, DEPTH
   190→  → Outputs: LOAD3D_CAMERA (position, orientation, focal_length, FOV)
   191→        │
   192→        ▼
   193→AdvancedCameraControlNode (ComfyUI-AdvancedCameraPrompts)
   194→  → Reads LOAD3D_CAMERA data
   195→  → Inputs: focal_length_mm (1-1000), object_scale_meters
   196→  → Outputs: shot type classification ("medium close-up", "wide shot")
   197→  → Outputs: camera angle description ("low angle", "bird's eye")
   198→  → Outputs: structured JSON camera metadata
   199→  → Optimized for dx8152's MultiAngle LoRA
   200→        │
   201→        ▼
   202→Prompt → ControlNet / LoRA conditioning
   203→```

   206→```
   207→CarWash-2 Hydra Viewport (REAL cameras)
   208→  → ARRI/RED/Sony sensor dimensions (not game camera)
   209→  → Cooke/Atlas/Zeiss lens projection (not pinhole)
   210→  → Anamorphic squeeze, real T-stops, breathing
   211→  → Depth/Normal AOVs through correct projection
   212→  → Outputs everything Load3D outputs PLUS:
   213→     - sensor_body: "ARRI Alexa 35"
   214→     - sensor_gate: "Open Gate 4.6K"
   215→     - sensor_dimensions_mm: [27.99, 19.22]
   216→     - lens_model: "Cooke Anamorphic/i 40mm"
   217→     - squeeze_ratio: 2.0
   218→     - t_stop: 2.8
   219→     - lens_metadata_protocol: "Cooke /i Technology"
   220→```

   222→**Integration strategy (two paths, both valid):**
   223→
   224→**Path A — CarWash-2 as upstream of existing nodes:**
   225→CarWash-2 exports LOAD3D_CAMERA-compatible data. The existing
   226→AdvancedCameraControlNode can read it and generate shot descriptions.
   227→CarWash-2 *enriches* the camera data with real specs that the existing
   228→node doesn't know about, but the basic position/orientation/focal_length
   229→contract is preserved. Zero changes to existing nodes.
   230→
   231→**Path B — CarWash-2 as custom ComfyUI node (future):**
   232→Wrap the viewport as a ComfyUI custom node (like Load3D but with
   233→real cameras). Output LOAD3D_CAMERA + extended cinematography metadata.
   234→Build a CinematographicCameraControlNode that understands sensor+lens
   235→combinations and generates richer prompts than the generic
   236→AdvancedCameraControlNode. This is the premium path — but it needs
   237→the standalone viewport working first.
   238→
   239→**Recommendation:** Build Path A first (standalone app outputting
   240→LOAD3D_CAMERA-compatible data). Prove the pipeline. Then Path B
   241→(custom node integration) becomes Phase 5 convergence work.
   242→

   244→```

   246→   compatible data. Check ComfyUI source: comfy/nodes/load_3d.py
   247→   or equivalent.
   248→
   249→2. Does AdvancedCameraControlNode accept camera data via API
   250→   (not just from Load3D widget)? If yes, CarWash-2 can inject
   251→   camera state directly into a workflow via the ComfyUI API.
   252→
   253→3. Can Load3D_Adv accept external image inputs for its passes?
   254→   If yes, CarWash-2 could send its Hydra-rendered depth/normal
   255→   as if they came from Load3D, plugging into all downstream nodes.
   256→```
   257→
   258→---
   259→
   260→### Phase 3: Scene Composition (Sprint 7-8)
   261→**Goal:** Drag-drop assets, basic transforms, scene save/load.
   262→**Energy:** Medium. Gaffer's scene graph patterns (BSD) are the reference.
   263→

   265→- [ ] Load USD/glTF assets via drag-drop
   266→- [ ] Basic transform gizmos (translate, rotate, scale)
   267→- [ ] Scene hierarchy panel (tree view of USD stage)
   268→- [ ] Save/load scene as USD file
   269→- [ ] Multiple assets in scene with independent transforms
   270→
   271→**OR-node approaches (any works):**
   272→- Port Gaffer's SceneView patterns directly (fastest)
   273→- Build minimal scene graph from scratch (more control, more work)
   274→- Use USD's built-in stage composition (reference/payload arcs)
   275→
   276→**Ship criterion:** Place 3 assets in a scene, frame with Alexa 35 + Cooke 50mm, render to ComfyUI, get a coherent generated image. Save scene. Reload. Same result.
   277→
   278→---
   279→
   280→### Phase 4: Polish + PoC Demo (Sprint 9-10)
   281→**Goal:** The demo reel moment.
   282→**Energy:** High dopamine. This is the payoff.
   283→
   284→**The demo:** "I'm looking through a Cooke 50mm anamorphic on an Alexa 35. I place a character in the scene. I hit render. ComfyUI generates what this shot looks like."
   285→
   286→**AND-node subtasks:**
   287→- [ ] UI polish (camera/lens dropdowns, render button, progress indicator)
   288→- [ ] Anamorphic visual characteristics as post-process (oval bokeh, horizontal flare)
   289→- [ ] Side-by-side: viewport wireframe | generated image
   290→- [ ] Performance: interactive camera manipulation at 30fps+
   291→- [ ] README + build instructions for collaborators
   292→
   293→**Ship criterion:** Screen recording that makes people go "holy shit."
   294→
   295→---
   296→
   297→### Phase 5: Convergence with Agent Track + Custom Node (Future)
   298→**Goal:** Agent can drive the viewport AND viewport ships as a ComfyUI custom node.
   299→**Energy:** Requires both tracks to be independently functional.
   300→
   301→**Subtasks — Node Integration (Path B from above):**
   302→- [ ] Wrap Hydra viewport as a ComfyUI custom node (like Load3D but real cameras)
   303→- [ ] Output type: LOAD3D_CAMERA + CARWASH_CINEMA (extended metadata)
   304→- [ ] Build CinematographicCameraControlNode (richer prompts than AdvancedCameraControlNode)
   305→- [ ] v3 schema compliance (stateless class interface, async execution)
   306→- [ ] Depth/Normal passes plug directly into existing ControlNet nodes
   307→
   308→**Subtasks — Agent Convergence:**
   309→- [ ] Viewport exposes a tool API (JSON-RPC or similar)
   310→- [ ] Agent gets a `viewport_camera` tool and a `viewport_render` tool
   311→- [ ] "Set up a medium close-up with anamorphic bokeh" → agent calls viewport
   312→- [ ] Generated image feeds back into agent's visual reasoning
   313→
   314→**This is the moat.** Nobody else has an AI agent that understands cinematography AND controls a real camera viewport AND conditions generative models on the result. This is where 16 years of Houdini + the agent work + the viewport converge.
   315→
   316→---
   317→
   318→## Sprint Cadence for Small Sprints
   319→
   320→Each phase breaks into ~2 sprints. Each sprint is scoped for a few focused sessions:
   321→
   322→| Sprint | Phase | Deliverable | Who Does the Work |
   323→|--------|-------|-------------|-------------------|
   324→| 1 | 0 | CMake + USD compiling on Windows | Claude Code (grind) |
   325→| 2 | 0 | Qt + Storm rendering a cube | Claude Code + you validate |

## Project: CarWash-2 | Status: ACTIVE (parallel track)
## Updated: 2026-02-19

---

## Questions for Claude Code (Agent Track)

Before building further on the viewport, we need ground truth on the agent's UI plan state. Paste these to Claude Code:

```
1. Do Phases 0-3 of the SUPERDUPER_UI_PLAN exist as shipped code?
   - Phase 0 (Recon) — any audit output?
   - Phase 1 (Sidebar Skeleton) — does a sidebar UI component exist?
   - Phase 2 (Backend Bridge) — does a frontend↔backend bridge exist beyond Graft A?
   - Phase 3 (DISCOVER Panel) — does any frontend panel render partner/community/core badges?

2. Grafts A-D shipped backend knowledge. What is the FIRST UI surface that can display it?
   Is it the agent's conversational responses? Or does it need a panel?

3. Is the agent currently capable of answering "what's the best 3D generator?"
   with the comparative knowledge from Graft C/D? Or is that knowledge
   injected but not yet routed to response generation?

4. 665 tests green — are there any test categories marked skip/pending
   that relate to UI rendering or frontend integration?
```

---

## Two Parallel Tracks — How They Converge

```
AGENT TRACK                          VIEWPORT TRACK
(ComfyUI-Agent / Super Duper)        (CarWash-2 / 3D Viewport)
─────────────────────────────        ──────────────────────────
Knowledge layer (Grafts A-D) ✅       Architecture blueprint
68 tools                              Hydra + Qt + Storm
DISCOVER/PILOT/BRAIN layers           Real camera system (ARRI/Cooke)
Conversational UI                     Depth/Normal → ComfyUI pipeline
                    \                /
                     \              /
              EXISTING COMFYUI ECOSYSTEM
              ┌─────────────────────────┐
              │ Load3D → LOAD3D_CAMERA  │
              │ AdvancedCameraControl   │
              │ ControlNet pipeline     │
              │ MultiAngle LoRAs        │
              └────────────┬────────────┘
                           │
                      CONVERGENCE
                     ┌────────────┐
                     │ CarWash-2  │
                     │ as custom  │
                     │ node with  │
                     │ real cams  │
                     │ + agent    │
                     │ tool API   │
                     └────────────┘
```

**Key insight:** ComfyUI already has Load3D → AdvancedCameraControlNode → prompt generation. CarWash-2 doesn't replace this — it plugs in as a premium upstream that adds real cinematographic accuracy. The existing `LOAD3D_CAMERA` data type is the integration contract.

**But that's Phase 6+ territory.** Each track ships independently first.

---

## Viewport Track — Phased Strategy

### Phase 0: Foundation (Sprint 1-2)
**Goal:** Qt window with Storm rendering a cube. Build system working.
**Energy:** Agent-team grindable. You validate it compiles + renders.

**AND-node subtasks (all required):**
- [ ] Fork CarWash repo, strip Houdini HDK dependency
- [ ] CMake links against standalone OpenUSD/Hydra (not Houdini's bundled USD)
- [ ] Qt window hosts OpenGL context
- [ ] Storm render delegate renders a UsdGeomCube
- [ ] Depth AOV renders to buffer (verify pixel values)

**Hardest branch:** USD/Hydra build system on Windows with Qt. This is the 60% calendar-time problem. Gaffer's CMake patterns (BSD licensed) are the cheat code. CarWash's existing build infrastructure transfers partially — strip Houdini, add standalone USD.

**Existing assets that transfer:**
- CarWash's 2,360-line ComfyUI client (WebSocket, HTTP, PNG encoding, base64)
- CarWash's CMake structure (adapt, don't rewrite)
- CarWash's framebuffer + FNV-1a determinism framework

**Claude Code task:**
```
Get OpenUSD 24.11 compiling on Windows with Qt6 and Storm.
Reference Gaffer's CMake patterns (BSD, github.com/GafferHQ/gaffer).
Port CarWash's CMakeLists.txt — strip find_package(Houdini),
add find_package(pxr). Target: render a UsdGeomCube in a Qt window
via Storm. No camera work yet — just prove the build pipeline works.
```

**Ship criterion:** Screenshot of a grey cube in a Qt window. Verifiable.

---

### Phase 1: Camera System (Sprint 3-4)
**Goal:** Real cinematographic camera with ARRI sensor + Cooke lens projection.
**Energy:** YOUR work. This is the unfair advantage. Agent teams implement, you direct.

**AND-node subtasks:**
- [ ] Camera prim with real sensor dimensions (Alexa 35: 27.99 × 19.22mm Open Gate)
- [ ] Projection matrix from real lens specs (Cooke anamorphic 40mm, 2x squeeze)
- [ ] Mouse orbit/pan/zoom interaction
- [ ] Camera metadata embedded in USD (sensor, lens, T-stop, focal length)
- [ ] Viewport matches what a DP sees through the eyepiece

**Camera database (you already know most of this):**

| Camera | Sensor W (mm) | Sensor H (mm) | Gate |
|--------|---------------|---------------|------|
| ALEXA 35 | 27.99 | 19.22 | Open Gate 4.6K |
| ALEXA 35 | 27.99 | 15.74 | 4:3 |
| ALEXA 35 | 27.99 | 11.81 | 2.39:1 |
| RED V-RAPTOR | 40.96 | 21.60 | Full Frame 8K |
| Sony VENICE 2 | 36.20 | 24.10 | Full Frame |

| Lens | Focal (mm) | Squeeze | Bokeh | Notes |
|------|-----------|---------|-------|-------|
| Cooke Anamorphic/i 40mm | 40 | 2x | Oval | /i metadata protocol |
| Cooke Anamorphic/i 50mm | 50 | 2x | Oval | |
| Cooke S7/i 25mm | 25 | 1x (spherical) | Round | |
| Atlas Orion 40mm | 40 | 2x | Oval | Budget anamorphic |

**Ship criterion:** Same scene rendered with Alexa 35 + Cooke 40mm anamorphic vs RED + spherical 50mm looks *cinematographically different*. The depth maps encode different projection geometry. Verifiable by visual inspection.

**Claude Code task:**
```
Build camera prim system on top of Phase 0's Hydra viewport.
UsdGeomCamera with custom projection matrix built from:
  - Sensor dimensions (width_mm, height_mm)
  - Lens focal length, squeeze ratio
  - Real T-stop for DOF (future)
Mouse orbit/pan/zoom. Camera dropdown: ARRI Alexa 35, RED V-RAPTOR.
Lens dropdown: Cooke Anamorphic 40mm, Cooke S7/i 25mm.
Switching camera+lens changes the projection matrix and viewport.
Store sensor/lens data as USD custom attributes on the camera prim.
```

---

### Phase 2: Render Passes + ComfyUI Bridge (Sprint 5-6)
**Goal:** Depth + Normal AOVs → WebSocket → ComfyUI → generated image displayed.
**Energy:** Mostly porting. CarWash's ComfyUI client code transfers directly.

**AND-node subtasks:**
- [ ] Depth AOV renders through the real camera projection
- [ ] Normal AOV renders through the real camera projection
- [ ] PNG encoding of AOV buffers (CarWash code transfers)
- [ ] WebSocket client sends buffers to ComfyUI API (CarWash code transfers)
- [ ] ControlNet workflow builder (CarWash code transfers — LTX-2 + ControlNet)
- [ ] Receive generated image, display in companion panel
- [ ] Camera metadata sent as prompt context ("Alexa 35, Cooke 40mm anamorphic, T2.8")
- [ ] **Output LOAD3D_CAMERA-compatible data** (see integration section below)

**Hardest branch:** Making sure the depth/normal passes encode the REAL projection, not a default pinhole. If this is wrong, the whole product thesis collapses — the AI gets a generic depth map instead of a cinematographic one.

**Ship criterion:** Send depth+normal from Hydra viewport to ComfyUI. Receive a generated image that respects the camera's perspective geometry. Verifiable.

**Claude Code task:**
```
Port CarWash's ComfyClient (WebSocket, HTTP, PNG encoding, base64,
workflow builder) into the Hydra viewport app. Wire Hydra's AOV system
to render depth + normal passes through the camera from Phase 1.
Send both passes to ComfyUI via the existing API. Build a ControlNet
workflow that conditions on depth. Display the returned image in a
Qt panel next to the viewport. Include camera metadata in the prompt.

IMPORTANT: Also output camera state as LOAD3D_CAMERA-compatible JSON
so it can feed into ComfyUI's existing AdvancedCameraControlNode.
See "Integration with Existing 3D Camera Nodes" section.
```

---

### Integration with Existing 3D Camera Control Nodes

ComfyUI already has a camera data pipeline. CarWash-2 should plug into it, not replace it.

**What exists today:**
```
Load3D node (built-in core)
  → Loads .gltf/.glb/.obj/.fbx/.stl
  → Three.js viewport in the node UI
  → Outputs: IMAGE, MASK, NORMAL, DEPTH
  → Outputs: LOAD3D_CAMERA (position, orientation, focal_length, FOV)
        │
        ▼
AdvancedCameraControlNode (ComfyUI-AdvancedCameraPrompts)
  → Reads LOAD3D_CAMERA data
  → Inputs: focal_length_mm (1-1000), object_scale_meters
  → Outputs: shot type classification ("medium close-up", "wide shot")
  → Outputs: camera angle description ("low angle", "bird's eye")
  → Outputs: structured JSON camera metadata
  → Optimized for dx8152's MultiAngle LoRA
        │
        ▼
Prompt → ControlNet / LoRA conditioning
```

**What CarWash-2 adds on top:**
```
CarWash-2 Hydra Viewport (REAL cameras)
  → ARRI/RED/Sony sensor dimensions (not game camera)
  → Cooke/Atlas/Zeiss lens projection (not pinhole)
  → Anamorphic squeeze, real T-stops, breathing
  → Depth/Normal AOVs through correct projection
  → Outputs everything Load3D outputs PLUS:
     - sensor_body: "ARRI Alexa 35"
     - sensor_gate: "Open Gate 4.6K"
     - sensor_dimensions_mm: [27.99, 19.22]
     - lens_model: "Cooke Anamorphic/i 40mm"
     - squeeze_ratio: 2.0
     - t_stop: 2.8
     - lens_metadata_protocol: "Cooke /i Technology"
```

**Integration strategy (two paths, both valid):**

**Path A — CarWash-2 as upstream of existing nodes:**
CarWash-2 exports LOAD3D_CAMERA-compatible data. The existing
AdvancedCameraControlNode can read it and generate shot descriptions.
CarWash-2 *enriches* the camera data with real specs that the existing
node doesn't know about, but the basic position/orientation/focal_length
contract is preserved. Zero changes to existing nodes.

**Path B — CarWash-2 as custom ComfyUI node (future):**
Wrap the viewport as a ComfyUI custom node (like Load3D but with
real cameras). Output LOAD3D_CAMERA + extended cinematography metadata.
Build a CinematographicCameraControlNode that understands sensor+lens
combinations and generates richer prompts than the generic
AdvancedCameraControlNode. This is the premium path — but it needs
the standalone viewport working first.

**Recommendation:** Build Path A first (standalone app outputting
LOAD3D_CAMERA-compatible data). Prove the pipeline. Then Path B
(custom node integration) becomes Phase 5 convergence work.

**Questions for Claude Code:**
```
1. What is the exact schema of LOAD3D_CAMERA? We need to output
   compatible data. Check ComfyUI source: comfy/nodes/load_3d.py
   or equivalent.

2. Does AdvancedCameraControlNode accept camera data via API
   (not just from Load3D widget)? If yes, CarWash-2 can inject
   camera state directly into a workflow via the ComfyUI API.

3. Can Load3D_Adv accept external image inputs for its passes?
   If yes, CarWash-2 could send its Hydra-rendered depth/normal
   as if they came from Load3D, plugging into all downstream nodes.
```

---

### Phase 3: Scene Composition (Sprint 7-8)
**Goal:** Drag-drop assets, basic transforms, scene save/load.
**Energy:** Medium. Gaffer's scene graph patterns (BSD) are the reference.

**AND-node subtasks:**
- [ ] Load USD/glTF assets via drag-drop
- [ ] Basic transform gizmos (translate, rotate, scale)
- [ ] Scene hierarchy panel (tree view of USD stage)
- [ ] Save/load scene as USD file
- [ ] Multiple assets in scene with independent transforms

**OR-node approaches (any works):**
- Port Gaffer's SceneView patterns directly (fastest)
- Build minimal scene graph from scratch (more control, more work)
- Use USD's built-in stage composition (reference/payload arcs)

**Ship criterion:** Place 3 assets in a scene, frame with Alexa 35 + Cooke 50mm, render to ComfyUI, get a coherent generated image. Save scene. Reload. Same result.

---

### Phase 4: Polish + PoC Demo (Sprint 9-10)
**Goal:** The demo reel moment.
**Energy:** High dopamine. This is the payoff.

**The demo:** "I'm looking through a Cooke 50mm anamorphic on an Alexa 35. I place a character in the scene. I hit render. ComfyUI generates what this shot looks like."

**AND-node subtasks:**
- [ ] UI polish (camera/lens dropdowns, render button, progress indicator)
- [ ] Anamorphic visual characteristics as post-process (oval bokeh, horizontal flare)
- [ ] Side-by-side: viewport wireframe | generated image
- [ ] Performance: interactive camera manipulation at 30fps+
- [ ] README + build instructions for collaborators

**Ship criterion:** Screen recording that makes people go "holy shit."

---

### Phase 5: Convergence with Agent Track + Custom Node (Future)
**Goal:** Agent can drive the viewport AND viewport ships as a ComfyUI custom node.
**Energy:** Requires both tracks to be independently functional.

**Subtasks — Node Integration (Path B from above):**
- [ ] Wrap Hydra viewport as a ComfyUI custom node (like Load3D but real cameras)
- [ ] Output type: LOAD3D_CAMERA + CARWASH_CINEMA (extended metadata)
- [ ] Build CinematographicCameraControlNode (richer prompts than AdvancedCameraControlNode)
- [ ] v3 schema compliance (stateless class interface, async execution)
- [ ] Depth/Normal passes plug directly into existing ControlNet nodes

**Subtasks — Agent Convergence:**
- [ ] Viewport exposes a tool API (JSON-RPC or similar)
- [ ] Agent gets a `viewport_camera` tool and a `viewport_render` tool
- [ ] "Set up a medium close-up with anamorphic bokeh" → agent calls viewport
- [ ] Generated image feeds back into agent's visual reasoning

**This is the moat.** Nobody else has an AI agent that understands cinematography AND controls a real camera viewport AND conditions generative models on the result. This is where 16 years of Houdini + the agent work + the viewport converge.

## Sprint Cadence for Small Sprints

Each phase breaks into ~2 sprints. Each sprint is scoped for a few focused sessions:

| Sprint | Phase | Deliverable | Who Does the Work |
|--------|-------|-------------|-------------------|
| 1 | 0 | CMake + USD compiling on Windows | Claude Code (grind) |
| 2 | 0 | Qt + Storm rendering a cube | Claude Code + you validate |

| 8 | 3 | Scene save/load + hierarchy | Claude Code |
| 9 | 4 | UI polish + anamorphic FX | You direct, CC implements |
| 10 | 4 | Demo recording + README | You |

1→"""SUPER DUPER UI -- aiohttp routes mounted on ComfyUI's PromptServer.
     2→
     3→Provides:
     4→  POST /superduper/chat   -- synchronous chat (request/response)
     5→  GET  /superduper/status  -- agent and connection state
     6→  GET  /superduper/ws      -- WebSocket for real-time streaming
     7→"""
     8→
     9→import asyncio
    10→import json
    11→import logging
    12→import queue
    13→import sys
    14→import threading
    15→import uuid
    16→from pathlib import Path
    17→
    18→from aiohttp import web
    19→
    20→log = logging.getLogger("superduper.routes")
    21→
    22→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    23→# Agent brain import (lazy — ComfyUI loads us before agent is on sys.path)
    24→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    25→
    26→_brain_lock = threading.Lock()
    27→_brain_ready = False
    28→_client = None
    29→
    30→
    31→def _ensure_brain():
    32→    """Lazily import the agent brain and create the Anthropic client."""
    33→    global _brain_ready, _client
    34→    if _brain_ready:
    35→        return True
    36→
    37→    with _brain_lock:
    38→        if _brain_ready:
    39→            return True
    40→
    41→        try:
    42→            # Add project root to path so `agent` package is importable
    43→            project_root = str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent.parent)
    44→            if project_root not in sys.path:
    45→                sys.path.insert(0, project_root)
    46→
    47→            from agent.main import create_client
    48→            _client = create_client()
    49→            _brain_ready = True
    50→            log.info("Agent brain loaded, Anthropic client ready")
    51→            return True
    52→        except Exception as e:
    53→            log.error("Failed to load agent brain: %s", e)
    54→            return False
    55→
    56→
    57→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    58→# Per-connection conversation state
    59→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    60→
    61→class ConversationState:
    62→    """Tracks one sidebar conversation."""
    63→
    64→    def __init__(self):
    65→        self.id = str(uuid.uuid4())[:8]
    66→        self.messages: list[dict] = []
    67→        self.system_prompt: str | None = None
    68→        self.busy = False
    69→        self.lock = threading.Lock()
    70→        self.workflow_summary: dict | None = None
    71→        self.missing_nodes: list[str] | None = None
    72→        self._workflow_hash: int | None = None  # skip reload if unchanged
    73→        self._first_workflow = True  # run missing-nodes check on first inject
    74→
    75→    def _build_system(self):
    76→        from agent.system_prompt import build_system_prompt
    77→        base = build_system_prompt()
    78→
    79→        # Append workflow context if available
    80→        extras = []
    81→        if self.workflow_summary:
    82→            s = self.workflow_summary
    83→            extras.append(
    84→                "\n\n## Current Workflow (auto-injected from ComfyUI canvas)\n\n"
    85→                f"Format: {s['format']} | Nodes: {s['node_count']} | "
    86→                f"Connections: {s['connection_count']}\n\n"
    87→                f"{s['summary']}\n\n"
    88→                "The workflow is already loaded in the PILOT engine. "
    89→                "Use PILOT tools (add_node, set_input, connect_nodes, "
    90→                "apply_workflow_patch) directly — do NOT ask for a file path."
    91→            )
    92→        if self.missing_nodes:
    93→            extras.append(
    94→                "\n\n**Missing nodes detected:** "
    95→                + ", ".join(self.missing_nodes)
    96→                + "\nWarn the artist if they ask about issues or try to execute."
    97→            )
    98→
    99→        self.system_prompt = base + "".join(extras)
   100→
   101→
   102→# Active conversations keyed by connection ID
   103→_conversations: dict[str, ConversationState] = {}
   104→
   105→
   106→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   107→# Workflow injection (sidebar -> agent state)
   108→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   109→
   110→def _inject_workflow(conv: ConversationState, workflow_data: dict) -> None:
   111→    """Inject live workflow data into agent state and conversation context.
   112→
   113→    Skips reload if the workflow hasn't changed (preserves undo history).
   114→    Runs find_missing_nodes on first injection (best-effort).
   115→    """
   116→    # Quick change detection via hash of sorted JSON
   117→    import hashlib
   118→    from agent.tools._util import to_json as _to_json
   119→    wf_hash = hash(_to_json(workflow_data))
   120→
   121→    if wf_hash == conv._workflow_hash:
   122→        # Workflow unchanged — rebuild system prompt (keeps context fresh)
   123→        # but don't reload (preserves undo history)
   124→        conv._build_system()
   125→        return
   126→
   127→    conv._workflow_hash = wf_hash
   128→
   129→    # Load into PILOT engine
   130→    from agent.tools.workflow_patch import load_workflow_from_data
   131→    err = load_workflow_from_data(workflow_data, source="<sidebar>")
   132→    if err:
   133→        log.warning("Workflow injection failed: %s", err)
   134→        return
   135→
   136→    # Summarize for system prompt
   137→    from agent.tools.workflow_parse import summarize_workflow_data
   138→    conv.workflow_summary = summarize_workflow_data(workflow_data)
   139→
   140→    # On first workflow injection, check for missing nodes (best-effort)
   141→    if conv._first_workflow:
   142→        conv._first_workflow = False
   143→        try:
   144→            from agent.tools.comfy_discover import handle as discover_handle
   145→            result_json = discover_handle("find_missing_nodes", {})
   146→            import json as _json
   147→            result = _json.loads(result_json)
   148→            missing = result.get("missing", [])
   149→            if missing:
   150→                conv.missing_nodes = [m.get("class_type", "?") for m in missing]
   151→            else:
   152→                conv.missing_nodes = None
   153→        except Exception as e:
   154→            log.debug("Missing nodes check skipped: %s", e)
   155→
   156→    # Force system prompt rebuild with new workflow context
   157→    conv._build_system()
   158→
   159→
   160→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   161→# Synchronous agent runner (called from thread)
   162→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   163→
   164→def _run_agent_sync(conv: ConversationState, user_text: str, msg_queue: queue.Queue):
   165→    """Run the agent loop synchronously, pushing events to msg_queue.
   166→
   167→    Events are dicts: {"type": "text_delta"|"tool_call"|"stage"|"done"|"error", ...}
   168→    """
   169→    from agent.main import run_agent_turn
   170→    from agent.tools import ALL_TOOLS
   171→
   172→    conv._build_system()
   173→    conv.messages.append({"role": "user", "content": user_text})
   174→
   175→    max_turns = 15  # safety limit per user message
   176→
   177→    for turn in range(max_turns):
   178→        try:
   179→            def on_text(text):
   180→                msg_queue.put({"type": "text_delta", "text": text})
   181→
   182→            def on_tool(name, inp):
   183→                # Infer stage from tool name
   184→                stage = _infer_stage(name)
   185→                msg_queue.put({
   186→                    "type": "tool_call",
   187→                    "tool": name,
   188→                    "stage": stage,
   189→                })
   190→
   191→            conv.messages, done = run_agent_turn(
   192→                _client,
   193→                conv.messages,
   194→                conv.system_prompt,
   195→                on_text_delta=on_text,
   196→                on_tool_call=on_tool,
   197→            )
   198→
   199→            if done:
   200→                msg_queue.put({"type": "done"})
   201→                return
   202→
   203→        except Exception as e:
   204→            log.error("Agent turn error: %s", e, exc_info=True)
   205→            msg_queue.put({"type": "error", "message": str(e)})
   206→            return
   207→
   208→    msg_queue.put({"type": "done"})
   209→
   210→
   211→def _infer_stage(tool_name: str) -> str:
   212→    """Map tool name to intelligence layer stage."""
   213→    understand = {
   214→        "load_workflow", "validate_workflow", "get_editable_fields",
   215→        "is_comfyui_running", "get_all_nodes", "get_node_info",
   216→        "get_system_stats", "get_queue_status", "get_history",
   217→        "list_custom_nodes", "list_models", "get_models_summary",
   218→        "read_node_source",
   219→    }
   220→    discover = {
   221→        "discover", "find_missing_nodes", "check_registry_freshness",
   222→        "get_install_instructions", "get_civitai_model", "get_trending_models",
   223→        "list_workflow_templates", "get_workflow_template",
   224→        "check_node_updates", "get_repo_releases",
   225→        "identify_model_family", "check_model_compatibility",
   226→    }
   227→    pilot = {
   228→        "apply_workflow_patch", "preview_workflow_patch", "undo_workflow_patch",
   229→        "get_workflow_diff", "save_workflow", "reset_workflow",
   230→        "add_node", "connect_nodes", "set_input",
   231→        "save_session", "load_session", "list_sessions", "add_note",
   232→    }
   233→    verify = {
   234→        "validate_before_execute", "execute_workflow",
   235→        "get_execution_status", "execute_with_progress",
   236→        "get_output_path", "verify_execution",
   237→    }
   238→
   239→    if tool_name in understand:
   240→        return "UNDERSTAND"
   241→    elif tool_name in discover:
   242→        return "DISCOVER"
   243→    elif tool_name in pilot:
   244→        return "PILOT"
   245→    elif tool_name in verify:

   256→    """Bidirectional WebSocket for real-time sidebar <-> agent communication."""
   257→    ws = web.WebSocketResponse()
   258→    await ws.prepare(request)
   259→
   260→    if not _ensure_brain():
   261→        await ws.send_json({
   262→            "type": "error",
   263→            "message": "Agent brain failed to load. Check logs.",
   264→        })
   265→        await ws.close()
   266→        return ws
   267→
   268→    conv = ConversationState()
   269→    _conversations[conv.id] = conv
   270→
   271→    await ws.send_json({
   272→        "type": "connected",
   273→        "conversation_id": conv.id,
   274→    })
   275→
   276→    log.info("WebSocket connected: %s", conv.id)
   277→
   278→    try:
   279→        async for raw_msg in ws:
   280→            if raw_msg.type in (web.WSMsgType.TEXT,):
   281→                try:
   282→                    data = json.loads(raw_msg.data)
   283→                except json.JSONDecodeError:
   284→                    await ws.send_json({"type": "error", "message": "Invalid JSON"})
   285→                    continue
   286→
   287→                msg_type = data.get("type", "")
   288→
   289→                if msg_type == "chat":
   290→                    content = data.get("content", "").strip()
   291→                    if not content:
   292→                        continue
   293→
   294→                    if conv.busy:
   295→                        await ws.send_json({
   296→                            "type": "error",
   297→                            "message": "Agent is still processing. Please wait.",
   298→                        })
   299→                        continue
   300→
   301→                    # Inject workflow if provided by frontend
   302→                    loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
   303→                    workflow_data = data.get("workflow")
   304→                    if workflow_data and isinstance(workflow_data, dict):
   305→                        try:
   306→                            await loop.run_in_executor(
   307→                                None, _inject_workflow, conv, workflow_data
   308→                            )
   309→                        except Exception as e:
   310→                            log.warning("Workflow injection error: %s", e)
   311→
   312→                    conv.busy = True
   313→                    await ws.send_json({"type": "stage", "stage": "THINKING", "detail": ""})
   314→
   315→                    # Run agent in background thread, stream results back
   316→                    msg_queue = queue.Queue()
   317→
   318→                    thread = threading.Thread(
   319→                        target=_run_agent_sync,
   320→                        args=(conv, content, msg_queue),
   321→                        daemon=True,
   322→                    )
   323→                    thread.start()
   324→
   325→                    # Drain the queue and forward events to WebSocket
   326→                    accumulated_text = []
   327→                    while True:
   328→                        try:
   329→                            event = await loop.run_in_executor(
   330→                                None, lambda: msg_queue.get(timeout=0.1)
   331→                            )
   332→                        except queue.Empty:
   333→                            if not thread.is_alive():
   334→                                # Thread finished — drain remaining
   335→                                while not msg_queue.empty():
   336→                                    event = msg_queue.get_nowait()
   337→                                    await _forward_event(ws, event, accumulated_text)
   338→                                break
   339→                            continue
   340→
   341→                        await _forward_event(ws, event, accumulated_text)
   342→
   343→                        if event["type"] in ("done", "error"):
   344→                            break
   345→
   346→                    # Send final assembled message
   347→                    if accumulated_text:
   348→                        full_text = "".join(accumulated_text)
   349→                        await ws.send_json({
   350→                            "type": "message",
   351→                            "role": "agent",
   352→                            "content": full_text,
   353→                        })
   354→
   355→                    conv.busy = False
   356→
   357→                elif msg_type == "approve":
   358→                    # Phase 4: patch approval
   359→                    pass
   360→
   361→                elif msg_type == "reject":
   362→                    # Phase 4: patch rejection
   363→                    pass
   364→
   365→            elif raw_msg.type == web.WSMsgType.ERROR:
   366→                log.error("WebSocket error: %s", ws.exception())
   367→
   368→    finally:
   369→        _conversations.pop(conv.id, None)
   370→        log.info("WebSocket disconnected: %s", conv.id)
   371→
   372→    return ws
   373→
   374→
   375→async def _forward_event(ws, event, accumulated_text):
   376→    """Forward an agent event to the WebSocket client."""
   377→    etype = event["type"]
   378→
   379→    if etype == "text_delta":
   380→        # Accumulate text (we send the full message at the end)
   381→        accumulated_text.append(event["text"])
   382→        # Also send delta for live streaming
   383→        await ws.send_json({
   384→            "type": "text_delta",
   385→            "text": event["text"],
   386→        })
   387→
   388→    elif etype == "tool_call":
   389→        await ws.send_json({
   390→            "type": "stage",
   391→            "stage": event.get("stage", "THINKING"),
   392→            "detail": f"Using {event['tool']}...",
   393→        })
   394→
   395→    elif etype == "error":
   396→        await ws.send_json({
   397→            "type": "error",
   398→            "message": event.get("message", "Unknown error"),
   399→            "recoverable": True,
   400→        })
   401→
   402→    elif etype == "done":
   403→        await ws.send_json({"type": "stage", "stage": "DONE", "detail": ""})
   404→
   405→
   406→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   407→# REST endpoints
   408→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   409→
   410→async def handle_chat(request):
   411→    """POST /superduper/chat -- simple request/response chat."""
   412→    if not _ensure_brain():
   413→        return web.json_response(
   414→            {"error": "Agent brain not available"}, status=503
   415→        )
   416→
   417→    data = await request.json()
   418→    content = data.get("content", "").strip()
   419→    if not content:
   420→        return web.json_response({"error": "Empty message"}, status=400)
   421→
   422→    # Use a temporary conversation for REST endpoint
   423→    conv = ConversationState()
   424→    msg_queue = queue.Queue()
   425→
   426→    loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
   427→    await loop.run_in_executor(
   428→        None, _run_agent_sync, conv, content, msg_queue
   429→    )
   430→
   431→    # Collect all text
   432→    text_parts = []
   433→    stage = "DONE"
   434→    while not msg_queue.empty():
   435→        event = msg_queue.get_nowait()
   436→        if event["type"] == "text_delta":
   437→            text_parts.append(event["text"])
   438→        elif event["type"] == "tool_call":
   439→            stage = event.get("stage", stage)
   440→
   441→    return web.json_response({
   442→        "role": "agent",
   443→        "content": "".join(text_parts),
   444→        "stage": stage,
   445→    })
   446→
   447→
   448→async def handle_status(request):
   449→    """GET /superduper/status -- agent and connection state."""
   450→    brain_ok = _ensure_brain()
   451→    return web.json_response({
   452→        "brain": "ready" if brain_ok else "unavailable",
   453→        "active_conversations": len(_conversations),
   454→        "conversations": [
   455→            {"id": c.id, "busy": c.busy, "messages": len(c.messages)}
   456→            for c in _conversations.values()
   457→        ],
   458→    })
   459→
   460→
   461→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   462→# Route setup (called from ui/__init__.py at import time)
   463→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   464→
   465→def setup_routes():
   466→    """Mount all SUPER DUPER routes on ComfyUI's PromptServer."""
   467→    try:
   468→        from server import PromptServer
   469→        routes = PromptServer.instance.routes
   470→        routes.post("/superduper/chat")(handle_chat)
   471→        routes.get("/superduper/status")(handle_status)
   472→        routes.get("/superduper/ws")(websocket_handler)
   473→        log.info("SUPER DUPER routes mounted: /superduper/chat, /superduper/status, /superduper/ws")
   474→    except Exception as e:
   475→        log.error("Failed to mount SUPER DUPER routes: %s", e)

1→# 3D Generation Workflows in ComfyUI
     2→
     3→## 3D Data Types
     4→
     5→ComfyUI 3D workflows use these connection types between nodes:
     6→- **MESH** -- 3D mesh geometry (vertices, faces, UVs). Exportable as GLB/OBJ.
     7→- **VOXEL** -- 3D volume data. Used for volumetric effects and splat-to-mesh conversion.
     8→- **POINT_CLOUD** -- 3D point cloud from Gaussian Splatting or NeRF reconstruction.
     9→- **TRIPLANE** -- Triplane feature tensor. Intermediate representation (e.g. Hunyuan3D sampler output).
    10→- **CAMERA** -- Camera position and rotation. Used by viewport and 3D control nodes.
    11→- **POSE** -- Body or hand pose skeleton. Used by VNCCS, OpenPose, ControlNet.
    12→
    13→These follow the same strict type matching as 2D types. MESH cannot connect to IMAGE inputs.
    14→
    15→## Hunyuan3D Pipeline
    16→
    17→Hunyuan3D (Tencent) generates 3D meshes from text or images.
    18→
    19→### Typical Node Chain
    20→1. **LoadImage** or **CLIPTextEncode** -- input conditioning
    21→2. **Hunyuan3DLoader** -- loads the Hunyuan3D model weights
    22→3. **Hunyuan3DConditioner** -- prepares conditioning for 3D generation
    23→4. **Hunyuan3DSampler** -- generates triplane features
    24→5. **Hunyuan3DMeshDecoder** -- decodes triplane to 3D mesh
    25→6. **SaveGLB** or **Preview3D** -- exports the result
    26→
    27→### Key Parameters
    28→- **steps**: 50-100 for quality, 20-30 for speed
    29→- **guidance_scale**: 7.0-10.0 typical
    30→- **resolution**: triplane resolution affects detail (256 = fast, 512 = detailed)
    31→
    32→### VRAM Requirements
    33→- 24GB+ VRAM recommended (RTX 4090 works)
    34→- Reduce triplane resolution to 256 for lower VRAM cards
    35→
    36→## 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS)
    37→
    38→Gaussian Splatting creates photorealistic 3D scenes from multi-view images.
    39→
    40→### Common Node Packs
    41→- **ComfyUI-3D-Pack**: comprehensive 3D toolkit
    42→- **ComfyUI-Hunyuan3D**: official Hunyuan3D nodes
    43→
    44→### Output Formats
    45→- `.glb` -- standard 3D interchange, viewable in browsers
    46→- `.ply` -- point cloud format, used by Gaussian Splatting
    47→- `.obj` -- classic mesh format with material support
    48→
    49→## Video-to-3D with Wan2.1
    50→
    51→Wan2.1 (Alibaba) supports video generation that can feed into 3D pipelines.
    52→
    53→### Wan2.1 Variants
    54→- **Wan-T2V**: Text-to-video
    55→- **Wan-I2V**: Image-to-video
    56→- **Wan-Fun**: Creative video effects
    57→
    58→### Integration Pattern
    59→Image -> Wan-I2V (multi-view) -> 3D reconstruction -> Mesh export
    60→
    61→## Model Directory Conventions
    62→- 3D models: `models/3d/` or `models/checkpoints/` (varies by node pack)
    63→- Wan models: `models/diffusion_models/` or `models/checkpoints/`
    64→- Some packs use HuggingFace-style directory downloads (multiple files per model)
    65→
    66→## Splat-to-Mesh Conversion
    67→
    68→Common friction point: converting 3DGS/NeRF output to exportable mesh.
    69→
    70→### Path A: ComfyUI-3D-Pack Marching Cubes (most established)
    71→1. Load splat (Load3DGaussian or equivalent)
    72→2. Marching cubes conversion -- resolution 256 (fast) to 512 (detailed)
    73→3. Optional mesh cleanup
    74→4. GLB export (SaveGLB)
    75→
    76→Pitfalls: low resolution = blocky mesh; GLB may lose UVs; large splats need downsampling.
    77→
    78→### Path B: Trellis2 Native Mesh
    79→Some models output MESH directly -- no conversion needed.
    80→
    81→### Path C: External Bridge
    82→Export splat -> process in Blender/Houdini -> reimport. Best quality when time permits.
    83→
    84→## Viewport & Control Tools
    85→
    86→These are not agent-operated. DISCOVER should surface them when relevant.
    87→
    88→### VNCCS (3D Pose Studio) -- @wildmindai
    89→- Full character posing, lighting, multi-pose, camera control
    90→- Use for: "pose a character", "set up ControlNet lighting"
    91→- Most popular 3D tool in ComfyUI ecosystem (3,126+ likes)
    92→
    93→### Action Director -- @wildmindai
    94→- Interactive 3D viewport, loads FBX/GLB, batch-renders ControlNet passes
    95→- Use for: "camera angle", "render depth map from 3D", "batch ControlNet"
    96→- Complements VNCCS: posing vs. scene/camera control
    97→
    98→### 3DView (Orion NodeFlow) -- @kakachiex
    99→- 3D model viewer inside the ComfyUI node graph
   100→- Use for: "preview 3D model", "view mesh in ComfyUI"

     6→RULES:
     7→1. NEVER claim to know about specific models from memory. ALWAYS use tools.

     9→3. When modifying workflows, ALWAYS show the proposed patch and get confirmation before applying.
    10→4. When something fails, read the error, check node compatibility, suggest fixes.
    11→5. Use extended thinking for: workflow design from scratch, debugging, architecture decisions.
    12→6. Use standard responses for: simple queries, status checks, model listings.
    13→7. If ComfyUI is not running, say so immediately. Most tools require it.
    14→8. Prefer /object_info over memory for node interfaces. It's always current.
    15→9. When suggesting new nodes/models, check if they're already installed first.
    16→10. Log key decisions and preferences to session notes (add_note) for continuity.
    17→11. At conversation end, save the session so the user can resume later.
    18→12. Use format='names_only' or format='summary' for large tool queries; drill down with specific tools.
    19→13. For workflow creation, prefer loading a template (list_workflow_templates) and patching it.
    20→14. Before executing, use validate_before_execute to catch errors early.

    54→

1→# Brain Layer Design — ComfyUI SUPER DUPER Agent v0.2.0
     2→
     3→> **Date:** 2026-02-11
     4→> **Status:** Design — pending implementation
     5→> **Author:** Brainstorm session (human + Claude)
     6→
     7→---
     8→
     9→## Executive Summary
    10→
    11→Add a **Brain Layer** on top of the existing four intelligence layers (UNDERSTAND,
    12→DISCOVER, PILOT, VERIFY) to transform the agent from a tool-using assistant (3.9/10
    13→autonomy) into a goal-driven, self-improving creative co-pilot with eyes.
    14→
    15→**Architecture:** Hybrid B+C — modules today, agent-ready seams for Agent SDK
    16→extraction tomorrow. Six new modules, ~18 new tools, bringing the total to ~52.
    17→
    18→**The six capabilities:**
    19→1. **Vision** — see and critique generated images via Claude Vision
    20→2. **Planner** — decompose goals into tracked sub-tasks
    21→3. **Memory** — learn from outcomes, recommend what works
    22→4. **Orchestrator** — coordinate parallel sub-tasks
    23→5. **Optimizer** — TensorRT/CUTLASS-aware performance engineering
    24→6. **Demo** — guided walkthroughs for streams/podcasts
    25→
    26→---
    27→
    28→## Architecture
    29→
    30→### Hybrid B+C Pattern
    31→
    32→Every brain capability lives in `agent/brain/` as a module registering tools through
    33→the existing pattern (`TOOLS` list + `handle()` function). Each module also defines an
    34→**Agent Contract** — a clean interface boundary for future Agent SDK extraction.
    35→
    36→```
    37→agent/brain/
    38→  __init__.py          # registers all brain tools
    39→  _protocol.py         # shared BrainMessage format
    40→  vision.py            # image analysis, quality feedback
    41→  planner.py           # goal decomposition, progress tracking
    42→  memory.py            # outcome recording, pattern learning
    43→  orchestrator.py      # parallel sub-task coordination
    44→  optimizer.py         # GPU-aware performance optimization
    45→  demo.py              # guided demo scenarios
    46→```
    47→
    48→**Design constraint:** Every brain module is stateless per-call but state-aware via
    49→persistence. Planner reads/writes goal state to disk. Memory reads/writes outcomes
    50→to disk. Vision and Optimizer are purely functional. This enables future extraction
    51→into separate Agent SDK agents without rewriting.
    52→
    53→### Protocol (`_protocol.py`)
    54→
    55→Shared message format for brain-to-brain communication:
    56→
    57→```python
    58→@dataclass
    59→class BrainMessage:
    60→    source: str          # "planner", "vision", "memory", "orchestrator"
    61→    target: str          # who it's for
    62→    msg_type: str        # "request", "result", "status", "error"
    63→    payload: dict        # the actual data
    64→    correlation_id: str  # links request -> response
    65→    timestamp: float
    66→```
    67→
    68→Today: dicts passed between functions (same process).
    69→Tomorrow: serialized JSON between Agent SDK agents (same structure, different transport).
    70→
    71→### Full Architecture Diagram
    72→
    73→```
    74→+-------------------- SUPER DUPER AGENT v0.2.0 ----------------------+
    75→|                                                                      |
    76→|  BRAIN LAYER (new)                                                   |
    77→|  +--------+ +--------+ +--------+ +-------+ +-------+ +--------+    |
    78→|  |PLANNER | | VISION | | MEMORY | | ORCH  | |OPTIM  | | DEMO   |    |
    79→|  |4 tools | |3 tools | |3 tools | |2 tools| |4 tools| |2 tools |    |
    80→|  +---+----+ +---+----+ +---+----+ +---+---+ +---+---+ +---+----+    |
    81→|      +----------+------+---+----------+-----+---+---------+         |
    82→|                   _protocol.py (BrainMessage)                        |
    83→|      +--------------+--+-------+---------------+                     |
    84→|  INTELLIGENCE LAYERS (existing, 34 tools)      |                     |
    85→|  +---------+ +----------+ +---------+ +--------+----+                |
    86→|  |UNDERSTAND| | DISCOVER | |  PILOT  | |  VERIFY    |                |
    87→|  | 13 tools | |  5 tools | | 13 tools| |  3 tools   |                |
    88→|  +---------+ +----------+ +---------+ +------------+                |
    89→|                            |                                         |
    90→|                  +---------v---------+                                |
    91→|                  |    TRANSPORT      |                                |
    92→|                  +---------+---------+                                |
    93→+--------------------+-------+-----------------------------------------+
    94→                  +--+-------v------+
    95→                  | ComfyUI Instance|
    96→                  +-----------------+
    97→
    98→TOTAL: ~52 tools (34 existing + 18 brain)
    99→```
   100→
   101→---
   102→
   103→## Module Designs
   104→
   105→### 1. Vision (`brain/vision.py`) — 3 tools
   106→
   107→**Purpose:** Give the agent eyes. See generated images, critique quality,
   108→compare before/after.
   109→
   110→| Tool | Description |
   111→|------|-------------|
   112→| `analyze_image` | Feed image to Claude Vision. Returns: quality score, artifact detection (banding, color shift, anatomy), composition notes, prompt adherence |
   113→| `compare_outputs` | Same-seed A/B comparison. Two image paths -> what changed, improved or not, specific differences |
   114→| `suggest_improvements` | Given image + workflow, suggest parameter tweaks (CFG, steps, sampler, prompt) |
   115→
   116→**Implementation:**
   117→- Vision calls use a *separate* Claude API call with the image (not the main
   118→  conversation context — images are large and would blow up the context window)
   119→- Uses `anthropic.Anthropic().messages.create()` with image content blocks
   120→- Returns structured JSON, not free-form text
   121→- Image paths come from `get_history` (execution outputs) or user-provided paths
   122→
   123→**The feedback loop:**
   124→```
   125→execute_workflow -> get output path -> analyze_image -> suggest_improvements
   126→-> apply changes -> execute again -> compare_outputs -> record_outcome
   127→```
   128→
   129→**Agent Contract:** `VisionAgent` receives image paths + workflow context, returns
   130→structured analysis. No PILOT or DISCOVER access — pure evaluation.
   131→
   132→### 2. Planner (`brain/planner.py`) — 4 tools
   133→
   134→**Purpose:** Turn high-level goals into tracked sub-task sequences.
   135→
   136→| Tool | Description |
   137→|------|-------------|
   138→| `plan_goal` | Decompose goal string into ordered sub-tasks with dependencies. Persists to `sessions/{name}_goals.json` |
   139→| `get_plan` | Return current plan with step statuses (pending/active/done/failed) |
   140→| `complete_step` | Mark step done, record what was accomplished, trigger next |
   141→| `replan` | Revise remaining steps when context changes, without losing progress |
   142→
   143→**Decomposition strategy:** Template-based pattern matching (deterministic, fast):
   144→

   146→GOAL_PATTERNS = {
   147→    "build_workflow": [
   148→        "identify_base_model",
   149→        "select_template",
   150→        "configure_base_params",

1→# ComfyUI 3D Viewport — Phased Strategy
     2→## Project: CarWash-2 | Status: ACTIVE (parallel track)
     3→## Updated: 2026-02-19
     4→
     5→---
     6→
     7→## Questions for Claude Code (Agent Track)
     8→
     9→Before building further on the viewport, we need ground truth on the agent's UI plan state. Paste these to Claude Code:
    10→
    11→```
    12→1. Do Phases 0-3 of the SUPERDUPER_UI_PLAN exist as shipped code?
    13→   - Phase 0 (Recon) — any audit output?
    14→   - Phase 1 (Sidebar Skeleton) — does a sidebar UI component exist?
    15→   - Phase 2 (Backend Bridge) — does a frontend↔backend bridge exist beyond Graft A?
    16→   - Phase 3 (DISCOVER Panel) — does any frontend panel render partner/community/core badges?

    18→2. Grafts A-D shipped backend knowledge. What is the FIRST UI surface that can display it?
    19→   Is it the agent's conversational responses? Or does it need a panel?
    20→
    21→3. Is the agent currently capable of answering "what's the best 3D generator?"
    22→   with the comparative knowledge from Graft C/D? Or is that knowledge
    23→   injected but not yet routed to response generation?
    24→
    25→4. 665 tests green — are there any test categories marked skip/pending
    26→   that relate to UI rendering or frontend integration?
    27→```
    28→
    29→---
    30→
    31→## Two Parallel Tracks — How They Converge
    32→
    33→```
    34→AGENT TRACK                          VIEWPORT TRACK
    35→(ComfyUI-Agent / Super Duper)        (CarWash-2 / 3D Viewport)
    36→─────────────────────────────        ──────────────────────────
    37→Knowledge layer (Grafts A-D) ✅       Architecture blueprint
    38→68 tools                              Hydra + Qt + Storm
    39→DISCOVER/PILOT/BRAIN layers           Real camera system (ARRI/Cooke)
    40→Conversational UI                     Depth/Normal → ComfyUI pipeline
    41→                    \                /
    42→                     \              /
    43→              EXISTING COMFYUI ECOSYSTEM
    44→              ┌─────────────────────────┐
    45→              │ Load3D → LOAD3D_CAMERA  │
    46→              │ AdvancedCameraControl   │
    47→              │ ControlNet pipeline     │
    48→              │ MultiAngle LoRAs        │
    49→              └────────────┬────────────┘
    50→                           │
    51→                      CONVERGENCE
    52→                     ┌────────────┐
    53→                     │ CarWash-2  │
    54→                     │ as custom  │
    55→                     │ node with  │
    56→                     │ real cams  │
    57→                     │ + agent    │
    58→                     │ tool API   │
    59→                     └────────────┘
    60→```
    61→
    62→**Key insight:** ComfyUI already has Load3D → AdvancedCameraControlNode → prompt generation. CarWash-2 doesn't replace this — it plugs in as a premium upstream that adds real cinematographic accuracy. The existing `LOAD3D_CAMERA` data type is the integration contract.
    63→
    64→**But that's Phase 6+ territory.** Each track ships independently first.
    65→
    66→---
    67→
    68→## Viewport Track — Phased Strategy
    69→
    70→### Phase 0: Foundation (Sprint 1-2)
    71→**Goal:** Qt window with Storm rendering a cube. Build system working.
    72→**Energy:** Agent-team grindable. You validate it compiles + renders.
    73→
    74→**AND-node subtasks (all required):**
    75→- [ ] Fork CarWash repo, strip Houdini HDK dependency
    76→- [ ] CMake links against standalone OpenUSD/Hydra (not Houdini's bundled USD)
    77→- [ ] Qt window hosts OpenGL context
    78→- [ ] Storm render delegate renders a UsdGeomCube
    79→- [ ] Depth AOV renders to buffer (verify pixel values)
    80→
    81→**Hardest branch:** USD/Hydra build system on Windows with Qt. This is the 60% calendar-time problem. Gaffer's CMake patterns (BSD licensed) are the cheat code. CarWash's existing build infrastructure transfers partially — strip Houdini, add standalone USD.
    82→
    83→**Existing assets that transfer:**
    84→- CarWash's 2,360-line ComfyUI client (WebSocket, HTTP, PNG encoding, base64)
    85→- CarWash's CMake structure (adapt, don't rewrite)
    86→- CarWash's framebuffer + FNV-1a determinism framework
    87→
    88→**Claude Code task:**
    89→```
    90→Get OpenUSD 24.11 compiling on Windows with Qt6 and Storm.
    91→Reference Gaffer's CMake patterns (BSD, github.com/GafferHQ/gaffer).
    92→Port CarWash's CMakeLists.txt — strip find_package(Houdini),
    93→add find_package(pxr). Target: render a UsdGeomCube in a Qt window
    94→via Storm. No camera work yet — just prove the build pipeline works.
    95→```
    96→
    97→**Ship criterion:** Screenshot of a grey cube in a Qt window. Verifiable.
    98→
    99→---
   100→
   101→### Phase 1: Camera System (Sprint 3-4)
   102→**Goal:** Real cinematographic camera with ARRI sensor + Cooke lens projection.
   103→**Energy:** YOUR work. This is the unfair advantage. Agent teams implement, you direct.
   104→
   105→**AND-node subtasks:**
   106→- [ ] Camera prim with real sensor dimensions (Alexa 35: 27.99 × 19.22mm Open Gate)
   107→- [ ] Projection matrix from real lens specs (Cooke anamorphic 40mm, 2x squeeze)
   108→- [ ] Mouse orbit/pan/zoom interaction
   109→- [ ] Camera metadata embedded in USD (sensor, lens, T-stop, focal length)
   110→- [ ] Viewport matches what a DP sees through the eyepiece
   111→
   112→**Camera database (you already know most of this):**
   113→
   114→| Camera | Sensor W (mm) | Sensor H (mm) | Gate |
   115→|--------|---------------|---------------|------|
   116→| ALEXA 35 | 27.99 | 19.22 | Open Gate 4.6K |
   117→| ALEXA 35 | 27.99 | 15.74 | 4:3 |
   118→| ALEXA 35 | 27.99 | 11.81 | 2.39:1 |
   119→| RED V-RAPTOR | 40.96 | 21.60 | Full Frame 8K |
   120→| Sony VENICE 2 | 36.20 | 24.10 | Full Frame |
   121→
   122→| Lens | Focal (mm) | Squeeze | Bokeh | Notes |
   123→|------|-----------|---------|-------|-------|
   124→| Cooke Anamorphic/i 40mm | 40 | 2x | Oval | /i metadata protocol |
   125→| Cooke Anamorphic/i 50mm | 50 | 2x | Oval | |
   126→| Cooke S7/i 25mm | 25 | 1x (spherical) | Round | |
   127→| Atlas Orion 40mm | 40 | 2x | Oval | Budget anamorphic |
   128→
   129→**Ship criterion:** Same scene rendered with Alexa 35 + Cooke 40mm anamorphic vs RED + spherical 50mm looks *cinematographically different*. The depth maps encode different projection geometry. Verifiable by visual inspection.
   130→
   131→**Claude Code task:**
   132→```
   133→Build camera prim system on top of Phase 0's Hydra viewport.
   134→UsdGeomCamera with custom projection matrix built from:
   135→  - Sensor dimensions (width_mm, height_mm)
   136→  - Lens focal length, squeeze ratio
   137→  - Real T-stop for DOF (future)
   138→Mouse orbit/pan/zoom. Camera dropdown: ARRI Alexa 35, RED V-RAPTOR.
   139→Lens dropdown: Cooke Anamorphic 40mm, Cooke S7/i 25mm.
   140→Switching camera+lens changes the projection matrix and viewport.
   141→Store sensor/lens data as USD custom attributes on the camera prim.
   142→```
   143→
   144→---
   145→
   146→### Phase 2: Render Passes + ComfyUI Bridge (Sprint 5-6)
   147→**Goal:** Depth + Normal AOVs → WebSocket → ComfyUI → generated image displayed.
   148→**Energy:** Mostly porting. CarWash's ComfyUI client code transfers directly.
   149→
   150→**AND-node subtasks:**
   151→- [ ] Depth AOV renders through the real camera projection
   152→- [ ] Normal AOV renders through the real camera projection
   153→- [ ] PNG encoding of AOV buffers (CarWash code transfers)
   154→- [ ] WebSocket client sends buffers to ComfyUI API (CarWash code transfers)
   155→- [ ] ControlNet workflow builder (CarWash code transfers — LTX-2 + ControlNet)
   156→- [ ] Receive generated image, display in companion panel
   157→- [ ] Camera metadata sent as prompt context ("Alexa 35, Cooke 40mm anamorphic, T2.8")
   158→- [ ] **Output LOAD3D_CAMERA-compatible data** (see integration section below)
   159→
   160→**Hardest branch:** Making sure the depth/normal passes encode the REAL projection, not a default pinhole. If this is wrong, the whole product thesis collapses — the AI gets a generic depth map instead of a cinematographic one.
   161→
   162→**Ship criterion:** Send depth+normal from Hydra viewport to ComfyUI. Receive a generated image that respects the camera's perspective geometry. Verifiable.
   163→
   164→**Claude Code task:**
   165→```
   166→Port CarWash's ComfyClient (WebSocket, HTTP, PNG encoding, base64,
   167→workflow builder) into the Hydra viewport app. Wire Hydra's AOV system
   168→to render depth + normal passes through the camera from Phase 1.
   169→Send both passes to ComfyUI via the existing API. Build a ControlNet
   170→workflow that conditions on depth. Display the returned image in a
   171→Qt panel next to the viewport. Include camera metadata in the prompt.
   172→
   173→IMPORTANT: Also output camera state as LOAD3D_CAMERA-compatible JSON
   174→so it can feed into ComfyUI's existing AdvancedCameraControlNode.
   175→See "Integration with Existing 3D Camera Nodes" section.
   176→```
   177→
   178→---
   179→
   180→### Integration with Existing 3D Camera Control Nodes
   181→
   182→ComfyUI already has a camera data pipeline. CarWash-2 should plug into it, not replace it.
   183→
   184→**What exists today:**
   185→```
   186→Load3D node (built-in core)
   187→  → Loads .gltf/.glb/.obj/.fbx/.stl
   188→  → Three.js viewport in the node UI
   189→  → Outputs: IMAGE, MASK, NORMAL, DEPTH
   190→  → Outputs: LOAD3D_CAMERA (position, orientation, focal_length, FOV)
   191→        │
   192→        ▼
   193→AdvancedCameraControlNode (ComfyUI-AdvancedCameraPrompts)
   194→  → Reads LOAD3D_CAMERA data
   195→  → Inputs: focal_length_mm (1-1000), object_scale_meters
   196→  → Outputs: shot type classification ("medium close-up", "wide shot")
   197→  → Outputs: camera angle description ("low angle", "bird's eye")
   198→  → Outputs: structured JSON camera metadata
   199→  → Optimized for dx8152's MultiAngle LoRA
   200→        │
   201→        ▼
   202→Prompt → ControlNet / LoRA conditioning
   203→```
   204→
   205→**What CarWash-2 adds on top:**
   206→```
   207→CarWash-2 Hydra Viewport (REAL cameras)
   208→  → ARRI/RED/Sony sensor dimensions (not game camera)
   209→  → Cooke/Atlas/Zeiss lens projection (not pinhole)
   210→  → Anamorphic squeeze, real T-stops, breathing
   211→  → Depth/Normal AOVs through correct projection
   212→  → Outputs everything Load3D outputs PLUS:
   213→     - sensor_body: "ARRI Alexa 35"
   214→     - sensor_gate: "Open Gate 4.6K"
   215→     - sensor_dimensions_mm: [27.99, 19.22]
   216→     - lens_model: "Cooke Anamorphic/i 40mm"
   217→     - squeeze_ratio: 2.0
   218→     - t_stop: 2.8
   219→     - lens_metadata_protocol: "Cooke /i Technology"
   220→```
   221→
   222→**Integration strategy (two paths, both valid):**
   223→
   224→**Path A — CarWash-2 as upstream of existing nodes:**
   225→CarWash-2 exports LOAD3D_CAMERA-compatible data. The existing
   226→AdvancedCameraControlNode can read it and generate shot descriptions.
   227→CarWash-2 *enriches* the camera data with real specs that the existing
   228→node doesn't know about, but the basic position/orientation/focal_length
   229→contract is preserved. Zero changes to existing nodes.
   230→
   231→**Path B — CarWash-2 as custom ComfyUI node (future):**
   232→Wrap the viewport as a ComfyUI custom node (like Load3D but with
   233→real cameras). Output LOAD3D_CAMERA + extended cinematography metadata.
   234→Build a CinematographicCameraControlNode that understands sensor+lens
   235→combinations and generates richer prompts than the generic
   236→AdvancedCameraControlNode. This is the premium path — but it needs
   237→the standalone viewport working first.
   238→
   239→**Recommendation:** Build Path A first (standalone app outputting
   240→LOAD3D_CAMERA-compatible data). Prove the pipeline. Then Path B
   241→(custom node integration) becomes Phase 5 convergence work.
   242→
   243→**Questions for Claude Code:**
   244→```
   245→1. What is the exact schema of LOAD3D_CAMERA? We need to output
   246→   compatible data. Check ComfyUI source: comfy/nodes/load_3d.py
   247→   or equivalent.
   248→
   249→2. Does AdvancedCameraControlNode accept camera data via API
   250→   (not just from Load3D widget)? If yes, CarWash-2 can inject
   251→   camera state directly into a workflow via the ComfyUI API.
   252→
   253→3. Can Load3D_Adv accept external image inputs for its passes?
   254→   If yes, CarWash-2 could send its Hydra-rendered depth/normal
   255→   as if they came from Load3D, plugging into all downstream nodes.
   256→```
   257→
   258→---
   259→

1→# CLAUDE.md — ComfyUI SUPER DUPER Agent
     2→
     3→> **Core Thesis:** We are not building plumbing. We are building the first AI assistant
     4→> that *understands* a VFX artist's ComfyUI workflow — and keeps up with the ecosystem they can't.
     5→>
     6→> **The Pace Problem:** New models drop daily. Custom nodes ship weekly. No artist can track it all.
     7→> This agent does.
     8→
     9→---
    10→
    11→## IDENTITY
    12→
    13→```
    14→YOU:        The VFX artist's co-pilot. Not a developer tool.
    15→AUDIENCE:   Lighting TDs, compositors, texture artists — NOT engineers.
    16→VOICE:      Knowledgeable colleague, not a terminal. Explain what you're doing and why.
    17→PRINCIPLE:  Driver, not generator. Small validated changes, never full workflow rewrites.
    18→```
    19→
    20→---
    21→
    22→## Project Summary
    23→
    24→ComfyUI SUPER DUPER Agent is an AI co-pilot for ComfyUI workflows. It uses Claude with
    25→60 specialized tools organized into two tiers: four intelligence layers (UNDERSTAND,
    26→DISCOVER, PILOT, VERIFY) and a brain layer (VISION, PLANNER, MEMORY, ORCHESTRATOR,
    27→OPTIMIZER, DEMO). Natural conversation drives workflow inspection, discovery, modification,
    28→execution, optimization, and learning. Built with the Anthropic SDK, httpx, and jsonpatch.
    29→
    30→The primary interface is MCP (Model Context Protocol) via `agent mcp`, making all 65 tools
    31→available to Claude Code, Claude Desktop, or any MCP client. The CLI agent (`agent run`)
    32→serves as a standalone fallback. Our value lives in the intelligence and brain layers above
    33→the transport.
    34→
    35→---
    36→
    37→## Commands
    38→
    39→```bash
    40→# Install
    41→pip install -e ".[dev]"
    42→
    43→# Run (requires .env with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY)
    44→agent run
    45→agent run --session my-project --verbose
    46→
    47→# Tests (497 tests, all mocked, <35s)
    48→python -m pytest tests/ -v
    49→python -m pytest tests/test_workflow_patch.py -v                              # single file
    50→python -m pytest tests/test_session.py::TestSaveSession -v                    # single class
    51→python -m pytest tests/test_context.py::TestTokenEstimation::test_simple_string -v  # single test
    52→
    53→# Lint
    54→ruff check agent/ tests/
    55→ruff format agent/ tests/
    56→```
    57→
    58→---
    59→
    60→## Claude Code MCP Setup
    61→
    62→This project is MCP-first: Claude Code **is** the agent runtime; these tools are its domain expertise for ComfyUI.
    63→
    64→**Install:**
    65→```bash
    66→pip install -e "."
    67→```
    68→
    69→**Configure** `.claude/settings.json` (or project-level):
    70→```json
    71→{
    72→  "mcpServers": {
    73→    "comfyui-agent": {
    74→      "command": "agent",
    75→      "args": ["mcp"],
    76→      "cwd": "C:/Users/User/comfyui-agent"
    77→    }
    78→  }
    79→}
    80→```
    81→
    82→---
    83→
    84→## Tool Usage Rules
    85→
    86→When using the ComfyUI agent tools via MCP, follow these rules:
    87→
    88→1. **NEVER claim to know about specific models from memory. ALWAYS use tools.** Model ecosystems change daily.
    89→2. When asked "what model should I use for X?" -- search first (`discover`), recommend after.
    90→3. When modifying workflows, ALWAYS show the proposed patch and get confirmation before applying.
    91→4. When something fails, read the error, check node compatibility, suggest fixes.
    92→5. If ComfyUI is not running, say so immediately. Most tools require it.
    93→6. Prefer `get_node_info` over memory for node interfaces. It's always current.
    94→7. When suggesting new nodes/models, check if they're already installed first (`list_models`, `list_custom_nodes`).
    95→8. Log key decisions and preferences to session notes (`add_note`) for continuity.
    96→9. At conversation end, save the session so the user can resume later.
    97→10. Use `format='names_only'` or `format='summary'` for large tool queries; drill down with specific tools.
    98→11. For workflow creation, prefer loading a template (`list_workflow_templates`) and patching it.
    99→12. Before executing, use `validate_before_execute` to catch errors early.
   100→13. Use `add_node`/`connect_nodes`/`set_input` for building workflows instead of raw JSON patches when possible.
   101→14. Never generate entire workflows from scratch. Make surgical, validated modifications.
   102→15. Every patch is validated before application. No exceptions.
   103→
   104→### Tool Overview
   105→
   106→| Category | Tools |
   107→|----------|-------|
   108→| **Live API** | `is_comfyui_running`, `get_all_nodes`, `get_node_info`, `get_system_stats`, `get_queue_status`, `get_history` |
   109→| **Filesystem** | `list_custom_nodes`, `list_models`, `get_models_summary`, `read_node_source` |
   110→| **Workflow Understanding** | `load_workflow`, `validate_workflow`, `get_editable_fields` |
   111→| **Workflow Editing** | `apply_workflow_patch`, `preview_workflow_patch`, `undo_workflow_patch`, `get_workflow_diff`, `save_workflow`, `reset_workflow` |
   112→| **Semantic Building** | `add_node`, `connect_nodes`, `set_input` |
   113→| **Execution** | `validate_before_execute`, `execute_workflow`, `get_execution_status`, `execute_with_progress` |
   114→| **Discovery** | `discover`, `find_missing_nodes`, `check_registry_freshness`, `get_install_instructions` |
   115→| **CivitAI** | `get_civitai_model`, `get_trending_models` |
   116→| **Model Compat** | `identify_model_family`, `check_model_compatibility` |
   117→| **Templates** | `list_workflow_templates`, `get_workflow_template` |
   118→| **Session** | `save_session`, `load_session`, `list_sessions`, `add_note` |
   119→| **Brain: Vision** | `analyze_image`, `compare_outputs`, `suggest_improvements`, `hash_compare_images` |
   120→| **Brain: Planner** | `plan_goal`, `get_plan`, `complete_step`, `replan` |
   121→| **Brain: Memory** | `record_outcome`, `get_learned_patterns`, `get_recommendations`, `detect_implicit_feedback` |
   122→| **Brain: Orchestrator** | `spawn_subtask`, `check_subtasks` |
   123→| **Brain: Optimizer** | `profile_workflow`, `suggest_optimizations`, `check_tensorrt_status`, `apply_optimization` |
   124→| **Brain: Demo** | `start_demo`, `demo_checkpoint` |
   125→
   126→---
   127→
   128→## Artistic Intent to Parameter Translation
   129→
   130→When the artist describes what they want in natural language, translate to ComfyUI parameters:
   131→
   132→| Artist Says | Parameter Direction |
   133→|------------|-------------------|
   134→| "dreamier" / "softer" | Lower CFG (5-7), increase steps, use DPM++ 2M Karras |
   135→| "sharper" / "crisper" | Higher CFG (8-12), use Euler or DPM++ SDE |
   136→| "more photorealistic" | Higher CFG (7-10), use realistic checkpoint, negative: "cartoon, anime, illustration" |
   137→| "more stylized" / "painterly" | Lower CFG (4-6), use artistic checkpoint or LoRA |
   138→| "faster" | Fewer steps (15-20), use LCM/Lightning/Turbo sampler, smaller resolution |
   139→| "higher quality" | More steps (30-50), enable hires fix, use upscaler |
   140→| "consistent lighting" | Add ControlNet depth/normal, reference image via IP-Adapter |
   141→| "similar to this image" | IP-Adapter with reference, or img2img with moderate denoise (0.4-0.6) |
   142→| "more variation" | Higher denoise, different seed, lower CFG |
   143→| "less variation" | Lower denoise, same seed, higher CFG |
   144→
   145→---
   146→
   147→## Model Family Quick Reference
   148→
   149→| Family | Resolution | CFG Range | Negative Prompt | Key Notes |
   150→|--------|-----------|-----------|----------------|-----------|
   151→| **SD 1.5** | 512x512 | 7-12 | Yes, important | Massive LoRA ecosystem, fast |
   152→| **SDXL** | 1024x1024 | 5-9 | Yes, but less critical | Base + refiner pipeline, better hands |
   153→| **Flux** | 512-1024 | 1.0 (guidance_scale) | No negative prompt | Uses FluxGuidance node, T5 text encoder |
   154→| **SD3** | 1024x1024 | 5-7 | Optional | Triple text encoder (CLIP-G, CLIP-L, T5) |
   155→
   156→**Compatibility rules:** Models within the same family are generally compatible. Never mix SD1.5 LoRAs with SDXL checkpoints. Flux has its own LoRA format. ControlNets must match the base model family.
   157→
   158→---
   159→
   160→## Workflow JSON Schema (API Format)
   161→
   162→ComfyUI API format is a flat dict of nodes keyed by string IDs:
   163→```json
   164→{
   165→  "node_id": {
   166→    "class_type": "NodeClassName",
   167→    "inputs": {
   168→      "literal_field": "value",
   169→      "connection_field": ["source_node_id", output_index]
   170→    }
   171→  }
   172→}
   173→```
   174→- Literal inputs: strings, numbers, booleans
   175→- Connection inputs: `[node_id_str, output_index_int]` tuples
   176→- The patch engine operates on this format exclusively
   177→
   178→---
   179→
   180→## Tool Redundancy Notes
   181→
   182→Some tools overlap with Claude Code's native capabilities. All are kept for domain-specific value:
   183→
   184→- **Filesystem tools** (`list_models`, `list_custom_nodes`, `read_node_source`): Overlap with Glob/Read, but provide ComfyUI-aware parsing (model type detection, node registration scanning). Keep.
   185→- **Discovery tools** (`discover`): Unified cross-source search (ComfyUI Manager 31k+ nodes, CivitAI, HuggingFace). Deduplication, ranking, installed-status. No native equivalent. Core value.
   186→- **Workflow tools** (entire PILOT layer): RFC6902 patch engine with undo. No native equivalent. Core value.
   187→- **Session tools**: Could potentially be replaced by Claude Code's own memory, but workflow state serialization is domain-specific. Keep for now.
   188→- **Brain tools**: Higher-order capabilities (vision analysis, planning, optimization). Core value, no native equivalent.
   189→
   190→---
   191→
   192→## Architecture
   193→
   194→### Four Intelligence Layers
   195→
   196→The agent's 44 intelligence + 21 brain tools are organized into four layers, each solving
   197→a distinct problem for the artist. The transport underneath is commodity plumbing.
   198→
   199→```
